body.rationale: Governing IPS status as given to me: ratified. Reviewers also treat the IPS limits as binding. I ranked for what the CIO can build from in a late-cycle regime, where covariance-based methods deserve more trust than return-forecast methods. 1) inverse_volatility: no hard IPS breaches, 14.8 effective N, -22.9% backtest drawdown inside the -25% limit, and no tuned parameter. Its reviewer found the weights check out. The weakness is that it ignores correlation across the roughly 43% in credit and sovereign sleeves, which is a known limit and not an error. 2) tail_risk_parity: covariance-only, 14.4 effective N, -20.9% drawdown, and its only breach is volatility at 7.67% against the 8% floor, which is a small shortfall that a blend can fix. The intra-category review found only a denominator quibble. 3) resampled_efficient_frontier: compliant and well diversified at 13.1 effective N, but the -24.84% drawdown is only 16bp inside the limit, as its reviewer noted, and the 8% volatility point was tuned. 4) cvar_minimization: compliant with the best drawdown among compliant names at -18.7%. It holds only 4 assets (2.9 effective N) and the volatility was walked up to exactly 8.00%, so it is a diversifying sleeve and not a core holding. 5) maximum_diversification: -16.8% drawdown and a covariance-only construction, which fits the regime. It breaches volatility and tracking error, and its reviewer says the TE breach is structural, so it only works in a blend. My first choice beats my fifth because inverse_volatility is IPS-compliant on its own with a simple, auditable construction. The fifth needs a blending partner to fix its 6.88% tracking error. I did not rank black_litterman or max_sharpe: the late-cycle evidence in §4.3 favours covariance methods over return forecasts, and reviewers flagged max_sharpe's drawdown breach and 3.1 effective N. I flag market_cap_weight at the bottom. Its -40.6% backtest drawdown breaches the limit by 15.6 points, and its CRO risk score is 0.80, far above the others. It is about 77% equity, and its reviewer shows that ETF AUM weights are not a market portfolio and double-count overlapping style funds. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble.
